findings: Intensive matching counts any counterpart per source frame without one-to-one or reciprocal coverage. One zero hash versus ten hashes(1zero,9far): AB accepted at fraction1,BA rejected at0.1 with threshold0/defaultmin_fraction0.3. Actual original function and ImageHash backend; supplied hashes, not decoded media.

Original _split_png_stream searches signature bytes without PNG chunk parsing. One real Pillow-decoded valid PNG with embedded signature in ancillary tEXt splits into two fragments. This helper control does not prove such metadata in actual ffmpeg output.
Malformed frame_hashes JSON raises JSONDecodeError out of whole visual-video operation, rather than isolating row.
Video process cache keyed on path/size/mtime and intensive_n; recipe/version or content observation not included. Source review only, no new video cache runtime.

Both ordinary and intensive video grouping retain greedy anchor/visited semantics; default5-frame matching requires4 matches within3sec duration. Intensive mode explicitly accepts start OR end and has no duration filter. These heuristics are not whole-video identity.
process_files/process_videos stat preparation catches PermissionError only; FileNotFoundError during scan-to-stat can abort. Source observation, not runtime control.
Reporting sorts best-quality candidate by pixel count, size then mtime; matching metadata does not establish perceptual quality or safe deletion.
